title: Narrow Red arrival windows using joint travel and layover paths
head: fix/red-joint-lap-paths
body:
Red forecasts spanning a future layover were adding travel uncertainty and wait uncertainty independently. Carry each sampled arrival into the existing lap-based wait calculation so early paths can wait longer and late paths can wait less. This narrows the measured longer-trip windows by about 13–14% with modestly better typical error; current historical tables and tracking are unchanged.

The change is limited to Red. The September 16–17 retrospective replay verifies identical tracking beliefs, both target occurrences, and full-server output parity. Independent next-lap review found improved typical error and proper interval scores, with some additional tail misses and lower-bound jumps. It does not fix the separate long-wait display ratchet or establish calibrated coverage.

Validation: 2,721 tests and server/web typechecks pass; other-route and fallback outputs are unchanged in regression tests. Full-server benchmark adds about 4 ms per poll on the local machine. Detailed measurements and limits are in docs/red-joint-lap-paths.md.
